title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Isidore de Offic. — bread/wine called body/blood; into sacrament not substance
pass_a_gloss: So that it ought to seem wonderful to no one if we summon as Possessor of the Truth to be propped up by us in this place one alone, ISIDORE, Bishop of Seville, writing thus in Book 1 On Ecclesiastical Offices ch. 8: Bread, because it confirms our body, is therefore called the body of Christ; but wine, because it works blood in the flesh, is therefore referred to the blood of Christ. But these two are visible; yet sanctified through the Holy Spirit they pass INTO THE SACRAMENT OF THE DIVINE BODY (not into the substance of the body and blood of Christ): For the bread which we break is the body of Christ, who says, I am the Living Bread; but the wine is His blood, and this is what is written, I am the true vine.
pass_b_english: So Strimesius summons one alone: ISIDORE of Seville (de Offic. Eccles. 1.8).

Bread is called Christ’s body because it confirms ours; wine referred to His blood because it works blood in the flesh — visible things that, sanctified, pass INTO THE SACRAMENT OF THE DIVINE BODY (not into the substance of body and blood).
source_text: Ut proinde nemini mirum videri debeat, si unum solum ISIDORUM, Episcopum Hispalensem, Veritatis hoc loco à nobis statuminandæ Possessorem advocemus, Lib. 1. de Offic. Eccles. c. 8. ita scribentem: Panis quia confirmat corpus nostrum, ideò corpus Christi nuncupatur, vinum autem quia sanguinem operatur in carne, ideo ad sanguinem Christi refertur. Hæc autem duo sunt visibilia; sanctificata tamen per Spiritum S. IN SACRAMENTUM DIVINI CORPORIS (non in substantiam corporis & sanguinis Christi) transeunt: Panis enim quem frangimus corpus Christi est, qui dicit, Ego sum Panis Vivus; Vinum autem, sanguis ejus est, & hoc est quod scriptum est, Ego sum vitis vera.

lemmas.gloss: INTO THE SACRAMENT OF THE DIVINE BODY

choices.english: into the sacrament … not into the substance
